arm.alt: Close-up of a forearm on the 1931 photograph, with a trail of blood running along it
arm.cap: Close-up of a forearm on the 1931 photograph, in negative so the blood shows light. It is turned the way the arm hung on the cross, wrist up, so the highlighted part of the trail runs straight down. Press the button: the arm turns about ten degrees and the other part runs straight down. Which part goes with which position is our reading. Arrows drawn by us; approximate. The blood is tinted red by us; approximate.

crown.text: On the forehead and all over the back of the head, small flows of blood start from many separate points, like punctures from sharp spines. They cover the scalp, not just a band around it. That fits a cap of thorns pressed onto the whole head better than the neat ring shown in most paintings.
crown.foreAlt: Close-up of the forehead on the 1931 photograph, with several small blood flows
crown.foreCap: The forehead: flows from several punctures, one shaped like the number 3.
crown.backAlt: Close-up of the back of the head on the 1931 photograph, with many small blood flows
crown.backCap: The back of the head: many separate flows above the neck.
crown.photoNote: Photograph by Giuseppe Enrie, 1931, shown in negative, so the blood appears light. Contrast raised by us so the stains are easier to see. The blood is tinted red by us; approximate.
crown.modelAlt: 3D model of a cap of thorns. Drag to turn it.
crown.modelCap: Drag to turn it all the way round. About half the thorns point inward, toward the scalp.
crown.label: Our own illustration of the idea. No one knows what the real crown looked like.
